utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honour. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Ivetic, we are still waiting for a response which it was announced you would give to us, 30 or 60 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, 30 days for the 11th Prosecution motion to amend the 65 ter list. I've checked and that was what we sought and that would be up until including 16 September 2013.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Having received now the Defence's response, the Chamber considers the large number of documents covered by the Prosecution's motion and therefore the Chamber grants the Defence request for an extension of 30 days and hereby gets the new deadline of 16th of September to respond. Having dealt with this, if there are no other preliminaries, could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given yesterday. That is that you will tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. Mr. Ivetic will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to now ask you something about the so-called secondary mass graves in this case. First of all, am I correct that in relation to the secondary graves, the information that the Prosecution has from its investigation is that these graves were dug in the time period of September and October of 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could now take a look together at P1481 in e-court and if we can have a look at page 7 of this document, and, sir, first of all I ask if you are familiar with this map or the information that is depicted therein.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can focus for a moment on the green dots, would you agree with me that the green dots are, in fact, these -- most of these secondary graves that we have been talking about?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in terms of the path taken by the Bosnian Muslim column leaving Srebrenica in July of 1995, and the places of known combat or ambush engagements experienced by that column, would you agree with me that the green dots depicting the sites of secondary graves are located nearby, within several kilometres of the sites where the column encountered combat or ambush engagements?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some of them, yes, but not all of them. Those on the north part of the map, they would be close to those sites, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, in the Popovic case, you were asked about assessments given by various sources for the combat casualties that were suffered by the Bosnian Muslim column that left Srebrenica for Tuzla in July of 1995. Do you recall that one of the items that you were presented with were some statements of Bosnian Muslims who had been members of the column and who had given assessments of the numbers of dead that they saw? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to revisit some of the testimony on that topic by looking at 1D1196, page 33 in e-court and that should correlate to transcript page 33599 of that transcript. And I'd like to focus on the first 13 lines of this transcript, sir, and if you can follow along, I'll have some questions for you after the -- after we review it. It reads as follows: "Q. Sir, is there any reason that you know of that we should doubt what this witness on Exhibit 2D669 had reported to the ICTY investigator in January 1996? "A. Yes. First of all, we have the number of surface remains collected in this area and you can find the total of them. It's a little bit more than 500 in this Pobudje area so far identified which you can find it in my report. Second, I'm wondering how accurate this number is. In order to assess the number, you need some special, I would say, training. It's not that easy. As police officer, I can say that there is a special training in order to assess how many people is gathered, for example, in one place. So -- and if you are not trained in that, so you can be -- you can be wrong easily." First of all, sir, do you affirm that this transcript excerpt accurately depicts your testimony on this point?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is such testimony truthful such that you would so repeat the same today if asked these questions?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, you talk here about special training as a police officer. So I'd like to ask you, sir, did you undergo any special training as a police officer to assess the number of people gathered or perhaps to assess casualties, the number of casualties, in the course of performing your duties?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not me personally during my career but some of my colleagues did attend such training or -- especially those who were dealing with public peace and order.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you permit that military persons might likewise have a training or developed skill necessary for their work to accurately determine and estimate how many people are gathered or how many people are injured or killed in a given area?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, it would be a speculation but some of them might be. It's the same like police officers. You see myself, I haven't received any training on that but only a specific certain of my colleagues they did receive such training so I would not generalise in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At the time that you gave the answer in the Popovic case that we have up on our screen that we just went through, did you at that time know what kind of career training the witnesses in question had, perhaps in the military, which might affect the reliability of the estimates that they gave as to casualties?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can finish up with the tail end of this page, it's on the screen, it's line 20 through 25, and the question is recorded as follows: "Q. Well, what endeavours did the Office of the Prosecution take in order to determine out of the numbers that you've put in your report, the 5300 or so, how many were actually as a result of casualties from walking over land mines? Did you do that analysis? "A. No, I did not. "Q. Do you know of anyone who did at the Office of the Prosecution?"

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "A. I think no one did it. "Q. Okay. How about did anyone do an investigation or at the least undertake the process to determine how many people from this military column that was leaving from Susnjari, how many died as a result of self-inflicted wounds or suicide? "A. No. There were no such investigation. "Q. Okay. How about as a result of these legitimate combat engagements? When the VRS attacked the legitimate column of military men, did anybody investigate to determine how many actually died as a result of that combat engagement? "A. No. I'm not aware of any such investigation. "Q. Not doing any of the investigation on at least those three and other areas, did you investigate whether or not any of those people who died as a result of either suicide, mines, land mines, or combat engagements, whether anyone buried those individuals? "A. Yeah. I was trying to find that fact but there were instances regarding this Glogova, what I mentioned with my corrigendum but apart from that, there was not a lot of such information." First of all, sir, does this selection from the transcript accurately record the answers that you gave to the questions?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you stand by those as being truthful such that you would so testify today?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to go through with you one of the -- actually both of the witness statements that were the subject of the questions posed to you in Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could first call up 1D1192, but if we could please not broadcast the same as I don't know if it's a person that has sought protective measures or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could first take a look at the title page together, sir, would you agree with me that this is a person who gave a statement to the Prosecution on the 23rd of August, 1995, and has his occupation listed as military and is a Bosnian Muslim in ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to look at the next page, which also should not be broadcast. I guess to be safe, none of the pages from this document should be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The second full paragraph of this page, we see that the man was a soldier and in fact a platoon commander in charge of a platoon of 33 men, himself included. Do you consider, sir, that a platoon commander has a bit more of a reason to be precise as to assessing the number and extent of either manpower or casualties than the average person?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to say. We would need to ask this specific question this particular person in order to find out the exact answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. At the bottom of the page, he starts giving his descriptions of what he saw and I'd like to go through that with you. It reads as follows: "As soon as I left with my group, the Serbs started machine-gun fire. I believe in order to force us in their territory. I heard also shelling in front of us, and I believe the Serbs shelled the units in front of me because I saw later a lot of dead bodies, killed by shelling. Ejub Golic was the commander of the Glogova unit who protected the rear, was killed later. After about 200 metres, people in the column in front of me stopped because they did not know the way and they had lost the sight of the brigades in front of them. There was a path of about maximum 1 metre wide. Those who had gone first had marked the way."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "And in Buljim, I and the others had been told not to leave the path and not to touch anything what was near that path, such as paper, tin cans, et cetera, because this was to mark the road in the minefield?" From this description, or from this part of the statement, is there anything that you consider renders this description to be unqualified or unreliable?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. That's his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to the next paragraph on page 3, so the first full paragraph at the top, I'd like to focus on that for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The description he gives is as follows: "I sent my father and brothers forward with the head of the column and told them I would stay to secure the rear. I waited about one half -- about half hour because these 2- to 3.000 people passed one by one. At that time, the Chetniks started aimed shooting at us with small arms. There were a lot of wounded and killed. Golic told us to go down and take shelter to a creek. He told us not to fire a single bullet because then the Serbs would take this as a breach of the agreement for the withdrawal, the ultimatum. There at the creek, I saw five bodies, two decapitated, the others mutilated, but I do not know if they died from shelling or if they had been slaughtered." Is there anything in this section of the statement which would give you reason to discredit the accuracy or reliability of the observations of this man?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that he appears to be reciting details in a manner consistent with military training as to the details to be remembered and to be reported?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you're asking for judgement of these kind of things, whereas the witness is not the one who should give that judgement but it's finally the Chamber in the context of the totality of the evidence. If you ask the witness whether he has any indication why this person would not have accurately told, then of course, the witness, unless there is any specific issue, has to answer by -- but if he has so -- the question, as long as it is, is there any fact to your knowledge, fine; if it is asking the witness for a judgement, not fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If we can -- I believe it's just the next paragraph now, if we can look at this one, it reads as follows: "About one kilometre further, every three to four minutes, one grenade was fired by the Serbs. We had a lot of wounded, civil and military. We tried not to leave behind -- leave anyone behind. During a rest period, I saw my father and brothers back. Then a soldier came and passed the order that all men who had a weapon should take position on the left and right flanks of the column to protect the people as much as possible. I saw one of soldiers pull out a hand grenade and activate it. He and three other people died. I saw several walk on mines, others lost their senses, killed themselves and even others. They went just crazy. Some run toward the Chetniks while yelling. I saw about ten people do this." Sir, is this section here consistent with the facts as concluded by the investigation of the Office of the Prosecutor as to the types of things that were occurring in the Bosnian Muslim column as it went towards Tuzla from Srebrenica in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these incidents did occur.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, is there any dispute about such incidents have occurred in the column?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, good morning to you. There is not a dispute per se as to the types of incidents that have occurred. The nature and the extent of these incidents is another issue, and I think that's where Mr. Ivetic may be toeing the line a bit close, but in terms of the types, we're okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether it amounts to 1.000 or 2.000 --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that's the issue, not whether it happened or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's correct. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could you please keep this in the back of your mind when you continue there because what seems to be the real issue is the number, not the type of incidents. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And we are getting to that. The next paragraph in the statement is where the witness -- where this witness that did the statement is giving a number and how he arrived at the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I'd like to have you follow along with me, sir. It reads as follows: "I caught up with my father and rest of the column. It started to get dark. Then suddenly the head of the column turned backwards and they screamed: Chetniks, Chetniks. The Serbs started shelling, fired hand-launched missiles during about half an hour. Until that time, we never had fired back. But at that time I heard the order: Let us open fire and try to break through. We opened fire and we managed to make a breach and we could move for about 500 metres. We came to a hill. There, I and others were ordered to go back and take the wounded. I went back also because I wanted to search my family members. I went from body to body and I believe there were at least 500 people there killed by the Serb fire." Now, is this part of this witness statement consistent with the findings of the OTP investigation?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, apart from the number, how he come up with this number, did he count them or what was the methodology used to find out how many people were there and did that, other parts might be consistent with our findings because we have in that area, in Pobudje area many people found or their remains were found on the ground, on the surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, if you remember, sir, the beginning of this part of the examination, we started with your answer in Popovic which indicated some special training would be required to reliably estimate the number of persons. If the individual went from body to body upon orders to take any wounded back, would you agree with me that such an approach would not necessarily need special training?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, the problem is that what he was focusing on at the time so he was focusing on wounded people, not on how many of them is -- and there, he hasn't been counting there. He hasn't been there to count them. Even when I'm talking about the special training, you are trained to do that and you are there to do that. For example, I mean, in competition or whatever, on sport event, you would be counting I mean how many people attended and you would be doing that on purpose. So that would be your main purpose, but obviously purpose of this individual was something else at that time, so it's really difficult to -- to say if this is an accurate number or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I would like to look at page 5 of this statement, the middle of the first paragraph, which reads as follows, sir: He's talking about the Hrncic area. He says: "I believe we were in the Hrncic area but I am not sure. I asked the ones who wanted to surrender to leave the weapons. Suddenly, about ten to 20 shells, I believe directly aimed, were fired at us. I believe it was WBR fire because all grenades arrived almost at the same time. It was a real massacre. There were many dead and wounded. I estimate about 150 in total. When another round was fired, I ran toward the woods to try to find shelter. I returned to the -- returned to the spot in order to try to find my father and brother. I saw a lot of wounded people, some were begging me to kill them. Other soldiers were looking for their relatives. One of them said he was from Srebrenica and said he knew the way towards the Udrc mountains." Now, again, he is talking about the Hrncic area. Is this description consistent with the findings of your investigation as to the types of engagement and casualties that were encountered in this area by the column?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Even in that area, which is part of Pobudje area, we -- there were some surface remains found, so there were casualties in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we look at the third paragraph, and I'm trying to see if I can condense it, if we can look at the first part of the third paragraph, and it reads as follows: "When we arrived, about three kilometres before Snagovo we met other soldiers who told us that the road there was impossible to cross since there were many troops, APCs and tanks. We returned back to Udrc. From there, eight of us went to Tisca and then in the direction of Kladanj. Near a tunnel by a creek, the person who knew the way told us to follow exactly his steps because the road was mined. I saw there around 25 to 30 bodies, most of them killed by stepping on mines, but I saw four of them who had been slaughtered and decapitated. We proceeded but one of my group stepped on a mine and three, four of us were wounded. One of the others said: You take care of the wounded, I will go to our lines and try to get help from our side. Then he left and about 200 metres further we heard a detonation. The three of us who were not wounded went to see if our guy had activated a mine but he had not. Then we heard screams, the wounded who had left behind -- who we had left behind were attacked by the Chetniks and -- and I do not know what happened to them. The Serbs caught us in a cross fire." Now, here we are talking about the region Tisca in the direction of Kladanj. Is this consistent with the findings of your investigation as to this region and the number and type of casualties that were occasioned in that area?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have some surface remains found in that area, not exactly in Tisca but close to Tisca, there were some collected from the ground over the years.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And we don't have to reed it but I can direct you to the paragraph before this one, he also in the last sentence of that paragraph, talks about: "On the way I saw several fresh graves, probably wounded who had died." Do you have any information at your disposal resulting from your investigations to either confirm or contradict the existence of fresh graves along the path of the column?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were fresh graves in -- up north in Orahovac. There is a -- this is the closest one and of course in Glogova, so these were the freshest, the graves, at the time. In that areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If you can assist us, this witness statement says that the -- on the way from Cerska to the Udrc mountains and after Udrc mountains to Kamenica is where he encountered these graves. Would that be the region that you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that would be in that area there is the Cerska grave, and from Cerska up to Udrc, no, there is no open graves at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I'm finished with this document. I'd now like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you one question, Mr. Ivetic? What do you expect the Chamber to do with the portions you read? The witness -- apparently in the statement a lot of details are given about what happened there and then this witness says, We found some surface remains. Do you expect the Chamber to rely on what you read from the statement? Or do you exclude that and say the Chamber should rely on what this witness told us, that is that there were surface remains found in area A, B or C? Because I'm asking you this because the person giving the statement has not attested to this statement. It raises quite a number of questions. There was a strong suggestion in your question, for example, that the witness literally meant to say that he went one by one to all -- to what he believed to be 500 persons. Now, whether he counted them or not was clearly an issue which cannot be clarified without that witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So my question is what do you expect the Chamber to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I expect to assess the evidence as a whole including this witness and his reliability. We started off with his testimony where he had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. My specific question is: Could the Chamber rely on the portions read apart from where the witness says, Well, we found some surface remains which is consistent with what the witness said, but all the other details and what happened and numbers and counting, et cetera, is -- should the Chamber rely on that or can the Chamber rely on that or even consider it at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Based upon this witness statement by itself, no. We hope to be bringing corroborating evidence of these facts later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine, but as matters stand now, therefore, the content of what that witness said in the statement to the extent not confirmed by this witness is not something the Chamber could or should rely on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can now call up 1D1191, and again this also should not be broadcast out of the abundance of caution for this person that was interviewed by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, just looking at the first page, can you agree with me this is another Bosnian Muslim who gave a statement in January of 1996 to the ICTY Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can move to the second page, and the third paragraph -- or, pardon me, the fifth paragraph from the top, which begins and reads as follows: "We found the traces of the groups in front of us and followed their path. We travelled like that until 1700 hours, when we arrived above the village of Kravica, in the forest between Kravica and Kamenica. We got an order coming from the front of the column to stop and take a break. We sat down. Five minutes later, we received another order that the civilians who were at the rear of the column should go first. I got up and started moving and passed by the column of people. I walked quickly during half an hour, passing by a lot of people, all of them were unarmed civilians and there was only one armed soldier every 50 metres guarding the sides of the column. I was moving towards the front when a very strong shooting started, again coming from all kinds of weapons. I noticed a big tree and took shelter behind. When I was there, I saw many people falling down hit by bullets. Everybody was dispersing and screams of pain from wounded people could be heard coming from all directions. Nobody could help them." If we could just go to the next page. "I stood up and saw many dead bodies around and also many wounded who had their limbs cut due to the shelling."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to end there and ask you, sir, is this consistent that there was this type of -- with the investigation that you or the Office of the Prosecutor undertook that there was this type of engagement above the village of Kravica, in the forest between Kravica and Kamenica?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would say yes, and the Prosecution does have even a video of this shelling going from the road, Kravica-Bratunac road, and this is exactly at that area. What's happening there, what we can see on the video, it's exactly the place or nearby where this witness is talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can go to page 4, the third paragraph on that page, this individual --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, Witness, did you find any surface remains in that area as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The -- many of them were found in that area as well. I think the biggest concentrations of surface remains were found or left there on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed. And they are accounted for in the report, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct, in annex B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could focus on the third paragraph, where this individual states as follows: "I went back to the forest and found there," and I guess I won't read the name out of an abundance of caution, "from the village of," and I won't read the name of the village but you can see it there. "He told me that many were still in the forest. We separated and my group decided to go to Zepa. I looked for somebody who was from Zepa to show us the way. I found," and again I won't read the name but you see it there, "who was from Zepa and who joined us." Another name I won't read, "who was a teacher, went with us. We decided to return to Srebrenica area and from there to Zepa. We first returned to Susnjari. We came to a creek above Susnjari and noticed that the village was burnt and that the cattle was walking around. We didn't see any soldiers so we went to seek for some food in the village. After we found what we needed, we started to walk. We spent a day in the forest above the village and observed the movements of the Chetniks. We continued towards Bukovic mountains to reach Suceska. During the night we found another group led by," and I won't mention the name of the individual or the village, "among them I knew also," another name, "from Srebrenica. All together we crossed the river Jadar and went to the village of Bektici. We arrived at the forest Susica. From there we could see Zepa and heard heavy artillery fire. We went to the village Vukoljin Stan where we met," a name, "who is the commander of the Mountain Battalion of Glogova. With this unit we went to Zepa where we stayed until the same event happened like in Srebrenica, the Zepa safe area fell." Now, first of all, sir, is this consistent with the investigation of the Office of the Prosecutor that a number of the men including fighters from the column that left Srebrenica in July of 1995 actually abandoned their trek and made their way back to Zepa?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct. There was even a Kravica survivor from there who went towards this -- towards Zepa and he ended up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As the results of your investigation, are you in a position to give a reliable number as to the number of Bosnian Muslim males that went to Zepa from the Bosnian Muslim column that left Srebrenica in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was reviewing once the number of -- or the estimate of how many individuals would have left for Zepa, so I don't recall as again specifically how many of those would be but maybe few hundreds, not more.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When you say few hundreds, 1, 2, 3, less than 5, more than 5? Could you --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be a speculation but it's definitely less than a thousand.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now, I'd like to go through just one more part of the statement with you of this witness -- of this person, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any specific information about the number of casualties of the group that headed for Zepa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, not in my report because my report is related to the events related to Srebrenica. Previously in my report for Tolimir trial I did have a section with remains or casualties from Zepa and -- but according to my understanding, most of those who left towards Zepa indeed found their way there. They were killed after, after the Zepa events so -- but they are not included in my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So they cannot explain -- if there were so little casualties, it cannot explain the number of persons found being dead, either surface or in graves? Is that -- I have to -- how I have to understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When you say that those that went to Zepa were killed after Zepa and are not included in your summary, where were those casualties of Bosnian males from Srebrenica that went to Zepa and that became casualties after Zepa, where were they buried?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them were just left on the surface, on the ground. They were found. They have around 30 or 40 so far identified. Some of them were executed and buried. A group of leaders from Zepa, we know for them. But for others, there were actually not that much casualties in Zepa than it was the case for Srebrenica. So it's altogether, let's say, up to 50 individuals so far identified in wider area of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would those individuals be on the list of missing persons from Srebrenica or from Zepa?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, some would have been reported as being missing from Srebrenica because that's the place where they were last seen. They, of course, then made their way down to Zepa and you would find them as missing from Srebrenica, but the place where they were found would tell us that eventually most probably they ended their way in Zepa and from there they have never made their way out to free territory. So it's not really a distinction there in those data, whether or not it is Srebrenica or Zepa-related victim. For some of them, it's known because they were only in Zepa, but those who migrated from Srebrenica to Zepa during those events it would be difficult to distinguish.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I appreciate that. Now I'd like to finish up with this page of the -- of this gentleman's statement as he then describes his trek from Zepa. And I can tell you that later on in the statement, this gentleman indicates that he only made it to the Muslim free territory in -- on 21 September 1995, so that all of these observations are at some point in time before then, although of course I would not know the specifics.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One moment, please. I think I can continue while my colleague consults.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "I fled with Hamdija's unit of 20 men. We left three days after the Chetniks entered Zepa. We went back and arrived in the village of Suceska where we collected some food. We continued and arrived in Susnjari where we stayed for a rest. Then we followed the path made by the column which had previously fled Srebrenica. We had walked for about four days. Coming down the Buljim mountain we found a lot of skeletons" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, please remain seated. Please remain seated. I gained the impression, Mr. Ivetic, that Mr. Mladic felt it important that you would receive the message or whatever it is immediately. Of course, Mr. Stojanovic is in the position to judge whether that is accurate or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour, if I may consult with Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, don't hesitate if there is any matter which needs to be brought to the attention of Mr. Ivetic immediately. I saw you were moving around a bit hesitant. Don't be hesitant. Just give it to Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, keep your voice down. Mr. Mladic, keep your voice down at all times. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I think I'd like to finish up with the quotation and then I'll deal with the issue that Mr. Mladic raised because we are in the middle of a citation and our time is approaching the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So I believe we had left off with the section: "We had found a lot of skeletons and parts of bodies of those who were killed on the way. Close from the spot of the first ambush, we found three survivors who had stayed there hidden for about 40 days. They refused to join us. When we then arrived at the forest where the second ambush occurred in order to try to identify some bodies. Bodies were still all around. I recognised the bodies of two men who were with me at the beginning, at their clothes and their bags. I searched for my brothers" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we turn the page, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "I searched for my brothers but did not find any of them. We did not count the bodies we saw but I would estimate that there were about 2 or 3.000 bodies." And, sir, I'd like to stop there and ask you is this consistent with the results of your investigation as to this region?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this Buljim region, I have to -- I have difficulties to trying to remember where that region is because it's not on my report as the region or place where the surface remains were found. So maybe you try to help me in which area this Buljim is. I can certainly find if I am provided with a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm told that that is right outside of the -- what was the protected enclave of Srebrenica near Sandici.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it's near Sandici then I'm -- certainly in that area because this is part of the Pobudje area. We do have many surface remains in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But again here the number, how accurate it is, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I appreciate that we have a question about the number. I'm just seeing about the rest of everything.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see we are at the time for the first break. I don't want to go over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we take the break first. But first, one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The issue you wanted to raise in relation to what Mr. Mladic told you, is that to be done with the witness and will it be done after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With the witness after the break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: After the break. Then we take the break first. Mr. Janc, we will take a break of 20 minutes. Would you please follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Before we get back to the statement of the individual that's on the screen, I'd like to return to Zepa and ask you if you're familiar with an event that occurred after the fall of Zepa, specifically when approximately 850 armed soldiers of the BiH army in Zepa, rather than submitting their weapons to the VRS, went with their weapons and passed over the Drina River into Serbia and surrendered at the village Sljivica and then thereafter many made their way to America and to Europe. First of all, are you aware of that event occurring after the fall of Zepa enclave?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that event. I'm not certain about the number of those soldiers but I'm certainly aware of the event, yes, that took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are you able to confirm or exclude any armed combatants from Srebrenica who had gone to Zepa may -- being a part of that group that did so, whatever the number may be?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not able either to confirm or exclude but I'm sure there were some.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And are you able to exclude beyond any reasonable doubt that any of those individuals might be on your list in your report?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How could they be, Mr. Ivetic, if you say they went to America and Europe, or some of them did, and they crossed into Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: They could still be listed as missing from Srebrenica where they originally originated from, Your Honours. If they never went back there, they could still be missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Listed in his report as missing, not as dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just to answer your question, on my report are only the individuals who have been so far identified. If they are still missing, if they are still missing, I have not included them into my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now, if -- if we could return to the document we have up on our screen, and if we can look at the middle --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone is open. Okay. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could look at the middle of the page that we have now, actually it's at the -- yes, it's right at the middle of the page, and the section reads as follows: "During the night we were spotted by the Chetniks and Osman was shot. I ran and bullets passed by. I could see the tracers. I arrived in a corn field and lost the others. I stayed a whole day there, just laying in the grass. In the evening I went back and travelled for four days before arriving at Udrc mountain. I met people there who told me that," and I won't read the name, "arrived there the day before. I found him together with a huge group of about 5 to 600. The next day the Chetniks started shelling and fired at us with armoured personnel carriers. Then they searched the mountain. We stayed hidden and then went to the village of Babici. Near of a water tap, we found six bodies of civilians near the tap. We noticed armoured vehicles and left and decided to return to Srebrenica." Is -- first of all, is this consistent with your investigation of the types of encounters or engagements that now these persons from Srebrenica who had gone to Zepa and now were leaving Zepa to follow the path originally taken by the column experienced following the fall of Zepa?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those who left Zepa, they did take different routes, south, west, east, and north.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is it consistent with your investigation that groups numbering up to 5 to 600 went along this route that this individual described and encountered combat engagements with the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm for this 500 individuals but there were certain groups who were heading north.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If you can clarify for the transcript, did you say "I can confirm" or you can't confirm?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Consultations should be limited to the real necessary during the hearings and should be postponed until a break. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, from this statement, we see that searches of the terrain, at least of the mountain, were being undertaken sometime after Zepa fell when this group of persons from Zepa fled. Can you conclusively exclude, with reasonable certainty, that these searches of the terrain conducted after Zepa fell, perhaps even into September 1995, according to this witness, resulted in human remains being found that were then collected and buried in the graves that are being called secondary graves which were dug in the month of September and October 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, just for my own guidance and from the excerpt that you read for this witness, I didn't see the name Zepa, and you're now talking about people coming from Srebrenica going to Zepa. Could you, just for my own edification, maybe explain the geography of those areas that are being mentioned here, particularly in relation to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you recall from the fourth page of this exhibit, this is the individual who -- from Srebrenica left with the column and then with several units went to Zepa because they could not break through and then stayed in Zepa until Zepa fell, and then went along the same path as originally taken by the Srebrenica column from Zepa and then encountered others, this group of 4 to 500 that were taking this same route. And I believe the geography that is identified in the section that we just read was Udrc mountain, and it says that the -- he met people there, numbering of 5 to 600, and then the next day the Chetniks started shelling and firing at them, and then the Chetniks searched the mountain. So we are talking about the region by Udrc mountain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks for that explanation which -- but I'm not quite sure whether what you referred to at page 4 is it because you're not showing us that page, you know, and -- but anyway, thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think the relevant part was read into the transcript on page 21, lines 18 to 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so. Thank you, Your Honour, for clarifying that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness very -- with a very short answer said "yes" upon your last question, Mr. Ivetic. Could we resume from there with the next question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that you cannot exclude that in addition to surface remains, some part of the list of persons you provide in your report as having been exhumed from graves may comprise these casualties from both the Srebrenica and Zepa exodus of males to Tuzla that were discovered upon the search of the terrain conducted after Zepa fell in September of 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have evidence that only in Glogova primary grave there were people buried who were collected from the ground along the road, Kravica or Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road. So we have evidence on that, that there was collection of those bodies along the road. Apart from that, there is no strong evidence or no evidence at all that any bodies which were -- remained in the forest that were ever collected. What we have in the northern part, we have primary graves and we have secondary graves. There is evidence on these secondary graves that they are -- to which primary grave they are connected, and evidence that in those secondary graves there are only individuals which are coming from those primary graves. This is based on physical evidence which is found during the exhumation and also on the latest DNA connections which I provided in this part of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, sir, that your DNA connections only match 6.3 per cent of DNA material from the primary gives to the so-called secondary graves?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And would you agree with me that there is evidence, written evidence, that asanacija or sanitisation of the terrain was ordered to be carried out in the various areas along the path of the Bosnian Muslim column's march towards Tuzla by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree with you that that was ordered. Whether or not that was actually executed, it's a different story. We don't have reports on actual search of terrain exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And so is it really your testimony that with a 6.3 per cent match of DNA from primary to secondary graves, evidence of orders of asanacija to be carried out, that you can exclude the possibility that some of the bodies that are buried were collected as part of a sanitisation or asanacija from the locations where combat took place and buried in these graves that are called secondary graves and which, in part, are secondary graves?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you answer the question. Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think Mr. Ivetic's question first assumes a fact that's not in evidence in this case. He's alleged that the DNA connection between primary and secondary graves amounts to 6.3 per cent but that assumes that there is DNA that can be matched --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- between primary and secondary graves to whatever -- whatever percentage, 100 per cent, 80 per cent, it assumes that that is possible and therefore there is DNA that's obtained from both graves that can be matched.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, this seems to be argument rather than an objection to the question. Second, if you say Mr. Ivetic's question first assumes a fact that's not in evidence in this case, is that not one of the specific elements of what makes the question a leading question, a leading question which is permitted in cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would submit, Your Honour, with all due respect, no, it doesn't. A leading question is a question that posits a conclusion but is not predicated on something that is not in evidence in the case. That's a different question. And a question that is predicated in the way Mr. Ivetic has phrased it is a misleading one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether it's misleading or not is another matter. I was taught, not coming from a common law jurisdiction, that a leading question can be defined as a question which either assumes a fact which has not yet been established or, second, that it may suggest an answer to that question. So two different types of leading questions. You, I think you referred to the one type and excluded -- I'm not going at this moment to enter into any further debate on the matter. Apart from that, the witness agreed to it, to the 6.3, before you raised the -- let me see.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Should have been in either the prior question or the question before that, Your Honour. I can find it. It's at page 29, lines 23, through page 30, line 1, of the temporary transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's leave it to that. The objection to the extent it was an objection is denied. You may proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you remember my question or would you perhaps like me to repeat it for you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would like to be repeated, but first of all, I rechecked my report and I can't agree with 6.3 percentage because we have in those primary and secondary graves, in total, 5.624 individuals identified. So -- and out of those number, 1852 -- for 1852 we found a connection between two -- at least two graves, if not more, and there were 1.000 connections between those graves. So this percentage should be much higher, if not -- it should be between 15 and 20 per cent of those cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm relying upon your report. Do you have page 5 of annex C in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And it says the total of DNA connections between primary and secondary are 386. So by math, from the --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's the summation, totals that you have it says: Total primary/secondary, 386. Am I correct in reading that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, you are referring to connection between primary and secondary graves only.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, yes. That's correct, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: To clarify the matter, Mr. Janc, on page 29, line 23, you was asked: "Would you agree with me, sir, that your DNA connections only match 6.3 per cent of DNA material from the primary graves to the so-called secondary graves?" And your answer was: "Yes, yes." Do you still stand by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, between primary and secondary graves, yes, direct link between those two sites, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, I think we're --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for my understanding, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The 6.3 per cent which you highlight that match, does it mean that there were any negative DNA conclusions to be drawn from others? I think we earlier -- and I think I asked a question about that. These links only refer to situations where part of the bodily remains were left at the site of the primary graves and that matching body material was found in the secondary graves. So it doesn't, at least that's my understanding, it doesn't say in any way that the -- that there is 94 per cent not matching or something of the kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's not my intention to say that there is 94 per cent not matching.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, and that it fully depends on whether to what extent, I would say, the primary graves were cleaned up totally or whether small portions remained there. That is at least my understanding of what the evidence is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Or the other reasonable alternative is that the bodies were not in the primary grave but only came in at the secondary grave, some of the bodies, those that are not matched to the primary. That's the other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes -- well, no, no, I'm not -- that's not what I said --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and I didn't exclude that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And my question, Your Honours, if I may just clarify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Give an explanation as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can clarify. My question is a follow-up to the witness's testimony at page 29, lines 10 through 22, where he says there is evidence in these secondary graves to which the primary graves that are connected that in these secondary graves are only individuals who are coming from these primary graves and this is based on physical evidence and the latest DNA connections. That's what this has witness said and that's what I'm asking, based upon this, is he really excluding the possibility that some of those remains in the secondary graves are remains that were not in the primary graves, and that's what direction I'm going.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a valid question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you answer that, sir? Let me restate it for you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Given that we agree that there is a DNA connection confirming 6.3 per cent of the remains that were located in secondary graves originated from primary graves, given that there is evidence or an agreement that there were documents ordering asanacija to be undertaken in the areas where we agree there was combat and we agree that there were casualties, are you really testifying here today that you exclude 100 per cent the possibility that some bodies were recovered in asanacija and buried in the secondary graves that were dug in September and October of 1995, that is, following the events that we have just talked about?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, for -- it would be really difficult to exclude for 100 per cent, with 100 per cent certainty, that possibility, but I would say based on evidence collected so far it would be very unlikely. So let me explain a little bit more on this. So we have to take into consideration the entire picture, not only what connections we have between primary and secondary graves because there is also importance what is happening, what connections we have between secondary graves. For example, if you have connection between primary grave and -- A and secondary grave B, okay? We have a link between those two, and then if you only have -- so it means one individual was found or body parts of one individual in both graves. Then if you have a connection of another individual which is between grave B and C, even that individual is linked back to the primary grave because the person B is coming obviously from the primary grave. So person C, even if you have only connection between two secondary graves, it's also linked back to the primary grave, to the same one, through -- that through that person B.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So in your hypothetical --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not hypothetical --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It is a hypothetical because you're using B and C. If you were using names it would not be hypothetical.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. In your hypothetical, B is the person, the one body that could be linked to the primary grave by DNA connections?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is one portion of it. Then you have analysis on soil and pollen samples so we know that certain secondary graves are coming from particular primary sites, so you have to take into consideration that. But in a way you are correct saying that it's difficult to say for everybody in those graves that are indeed coming from the primary graves, just based on the DNA connections.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So in order to -- in order to establish the clear picture, further analysis will be needed, deep analysis. I accept that. And as I was talking to the representatives from the ICMP when preparing this report, so they were telling -- telling me that they are putting together a kind of a sequence chart. So what they are doing is -- first of all, we have to understand that in each grave, secondary grave, you will usually find that there were several deposits inside the grave which means one deposit is one truck offload, so one transportation of bodies, one deposit. So what they are doing now is they are trying to establish which secondary graves have been filled first and then which -- what was the sequence of those -- of those events, so they are trying to find the links between them and they are doing that. And they are quite close to complete the -- their analysis. They are not yet finished. I asked for their report, or preliminary report on this issue, I haven't received one. Because it's a time consuming job because first of all, you have to know within -- if you're talking about one deposit which body parts were found within that deposit and then you link that back to the primary graves. So in order to be 100 per cent certain, one would need to do this analysis. So as I told you, you know, the Prosecution, the OTP, because I've been looking for this information already before, particularly if I can find information which body parts have been found in -- as part of certain deposit within the secondary grave, okay, I didn't find that information, but obviously the ICMP does have this information available and this is analysis they have been doing now for quite -- quite some time. And based on this analysis we will be much closer to the -- to the picture whether or not all of them are indeed related to or coming from the primary graves based on DNA connections again. I'm emphasising. However, again, if you check the -- my report, the charts, which we have been looking at yesterday -- I don't know maybe we could upload one if possible, to be easier to explain but we can go, for example, chart C, chart number 2, and have Branjevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The exhibit number is P1987.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It should be the fifth page from the end in e-court is chart number 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. It's the one after, please. Next page, okay. So what we have here, you have connections related to Branjevo primary and secondary graves on the -- and the right-hand side Kozluk. They are both along the Cancari Road. Based on the connections we can see and we can exclude, not only based on the connections, also based on evidence we have, that re-exhumations were done at different time. So one was done after another. I think Kozluk was first and only then Branjevo. So there is no sequence between those two. And based on this chart, you can also conclude that this is or, you know, establish that was indeed the case. Why? Because if they were done simultaneously, for example, theoretically speaking, again, and, for example, part of the bodies were taken from Kozluk and part of the bodies on the same truck from Branjevo and then deposited into the secondary grave, you would find now connections, for example, between Cancari 1 and Cancari 5, or there would be at least strong connections between those two.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And this is all theoretically speaking as you indicated?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not theoretically but that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's your words, theoretically speaking.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Theoretically speaking, okay, but let me correct myself in saying it --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you have evidence that the same truck was used --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could you allow the witness to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- complete his answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I'm saying here, if there was indeed mixture of bodies on the same truck, the connections would appear here on these charts but we have no strong connections between two group of -- groups of graves. So which basically means that Kozluk has been re-exhumed and the bodies were taken from Kozluk to Cancari secondary graves. After that, we have Branjevo and re-exhumation done there, and bodies were taken from Branjevo to secondary graves. If there was a continuation even, for example, one grave they -- they -- okay, they -- they finished the work at Kozluk and then the bodies would be taken from there to secondary mass grave and the mass grave, secondary mass grave was not full and they would continue job with Branjevo and bring the bodies from Branjevo into the same secondary grave, I'm sure there would be a connection, strong connection, for example, between two secondary graves, one in Branjevo and the other in Kozluk, but we don't have these connections. And it's the same if we go into the other chart, it will be the same, you see you don't have strong connections between the graves, which is telling us or which is a kind of evidence that those graves were filled up at one -- at one time, one per time, and they were not mixed with other individuals. Of course, of course, you know, in order to exclude your suggestion, that there would be -- there would be individuals taken from the woods, you would need, you know, further analysis which I have been talking about. But based on what I can see and what evidence have been so far adduced from various sources, that would be very, very unlikely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, before we continue, you may have confused the witness to some extent when you referred to the 6.3 per cent where the witness's testimony was that it was DNA connections and physical evidence. You just left out part of the witness's answer about the physical evidence and I think it has now been restored. It would have been better to avoid that. I raise this issue, and then take you back to yesterday where you did put to the witness the evidence of another witness, Witness RM306, and then you said, "who testified that pursuant to the legal obligations of the SFRY Law on Civil Protection," and you referred to the transcript page, "the bodies and remains recovered by asanacija would be buried in communal or mass graves rather than individual graves." And then the answer is irrelevant, but you misrepresented the evidence of Witness RM306, who didn't say this, on pages 11464 to 11465. He said, as a matter of fact, that the rule was that they should be buried in individual graves, in individual graves, that he wasn't certain that this was -- or at least he had doubts on whether it was done at any point in time. And at least on those pages, I cannot find that the bodies and remains recovered by asanacija would be buried in relation to, as you introduced it, pursuant to the legal obligations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The term "communal graves" is right there in the transcript, Your Honour. I can't pull it up now but that's where I got the question from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not inviting you to have a debate on the matter. I just want to point out to you that linking what was in accordance with the legal obligations and what happened in reality and mixing it up results in a -- at least partial misrepresentation of what the witness said. Now, the witness couldn't answer the question so there is no issue, but would you be please be very precise in any reference to either an answer this witness gives or an answer given by another witness so as to avoid any confusion. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And I must correct Your Honour that at transcript page 33, line 8, I gave credit to the witness for saying physical evidence and DNA connections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I said you may proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Now, I'd like to turn to 1D1196, page 77, in e-court. I apologise, it's going to be page 78. Again, 1D1196, page 78.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I'd like to focus on lines 8 through 19 with you, sir. This is from your transcript -- your testimony in the Popovic case. And reads as follows: "Q. So Budak is partially a primary grave, not in relation to this but Budak is a primary grave? "A. Actually, where secondary grave Budak 1 is located there is a Muslim grave, yes, next to it. "Q. Just one more question about this proposition that I made. It's a very reasonable possibility that those bodies were buried there, isn't it? "A. Which bodies you mean? "Q. I'm talking about the bodies collected in the woods in the area we have just discussed, Buljim, Kamenica, Pobudje, and so on. "A. Yes. If they were collected, those were buried somewhere for sure." Is this testimony accurately depicting the answers that you gave in the Popovic case to these questions?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you stand by the same as being truthful such that you would so testify today?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to look at 1D1195 -- actually strike that. We've already gotten that. Skip that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you testified about the Bljeceva grave being mixed with bodies from 1992 and 1995 and I would like to ask you a few follow-up questions in relation to that site. When you say that there were some bodies from a 1992 incident, would those bodies have come from the municipality of Bratunac relating to an incident at the Vuk Karadzic school in 1992? Is that what you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. That's the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we can please return to P1983, which was used with you yesterday. And page 4 in English, page 5 in the B/C/S, and it is again paragraph 10 which we were looking at yesterday. And paragraph 10 is where we looked at yesterday where it identifies that certain of the bodies on top dated from 1992 and others were 1995 were found at the bottom, I believe, of the grave. Now, I have a question for you. How many of the bodies from this site did you exclude as dating from 1992? Was it 50 or 80 or --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the number is around 100.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. It is about around 100?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Because in paragraph 4 of the document before us, it talks about 80 of these, approximately 80 bodies, that were in JNA body bags. Are those the ones that you excluded from this site or were there others?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are the ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So is it 100 or is it approximately 80?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's around 80 or 90, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, RM306 testified at our trial at transcript page 11481 through 11483, that he believed there were 100 to 150 bodies from 1992 which were removed and taken by Momir Nikolic. So the question I have for you is as follows: Can you exclude the possibility that the difference between the two numbers, that is the approximately 80 that were confirmed to be from 1992 and excluded, and the 100 to 150 that RM306 talks about, again we can't get an exact number, of course, but can you exclude the possibility that some number, perhaps as many as 60 or 70, dated from 1992 but were not excluded from your list based upon the testimony of RM306?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's included in my report are only victims which are related to Srebrenica events which were found or rather to say their body parts which were found in that mixed Bljeceva 1 grave and we have even DNA connections back to the primary Glogova grave and other graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to take a look at 1D1196, page 59 in e-court, which should correlate to transcript page 33625.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could focus on line 17 onward, I'd like to go over with you some of the testimony that you gave in this case to see if it is accurate? "Q. Okay. Did you review the pathology reports as to the cause and manner of death of the bodies that they did identify? "A. Yes, some of them, but not all of them. "Q. Excluding Kravica and Glogova, and excluding the two sites where we saw a significant amount of ligatures and blindfolds, do you agree with me that the cause and manner of death identified by the pathologist is vague? "A. I can't comment on that. "Q. Well, why not? You're an investigator. You gave them the" - and if we can turn to the next page - "direction to provide that information. If they say someone died as a result of a bullet wound, does that answer the question as to whether or not that person died from a self-inflicted wound? A wound from one of his colleagues? A wound from a combat engagement? Or a wound from an executor? All those four or five possibilities exist, do they not? "A. Yes, they do. But now, in order to -- to clarify the issue, you have to look into this particular case from different perspectives. You have to find more, for example, information about this particular individual, not only the reports, also the information statements and whatever evidence you can find on this person and then you can maybe perhaps establish the manner and cause of death. "Q. So you are saying, sir, that in fact you think it may not be vague but that it's incomplete? "A. Yes, perhaps. "Q. Well, try to be more definitive. You're an investigator giving evidence in an International Criminal Tribunal. You made a report in this case, not perhaps, it's without a doubt, isn't it, that the path report does not exclude or rule out any of the possibilities that I'm suggesting, that the numbers that you've given us are indeed inflated and included individuals who died as a result of sustaining injuries from land mines, self-inflicted wounds, and/or injuries from legitimate combat engagements? "A. Yes, you're right." Sir, can you confirm if this section of the transcript appears to accurately record the answers that you gave to the questions posed?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you stand by those answers as truthful such that you would so testify today the same way?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but there was -- for this last section it's a compound question and what I answered here and it was -- I think I've been asked on redirect again --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the same what was meant here, I was asked if these numbers were inflated and then you see it continues. My response was to that second part yes, but whether or not the -- my numbers were inflated, you know, my answer on response was later no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to look at document 25555, 25.555, from the Prosecution's 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, now that we have it on the screen, can you confirm for us whether as part of your investigation you had a chance to review and consider this UN document dated 17 July 1995 and updating the situation as to Srebrenica and Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, most probably yes, let's say. I cannot confirm really. I would need to go through, but most probably I did see this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And as part of your investigations are you familiar with the individual who drafted this report, a Mr. Ken Biser who is identified as the SCvAO Sector North-East Tuzla? Are you familiar with that -- with that person or that title designation within the --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can please move to page 2 of the document, and item number 1, I'd like to just have one or two questions about what is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you can follow along with me, sir, it says: "Escapees from Srebrenica have arrived at Tuzla airbase to join up with their families. UNMOs, civil affairs and others have spoken separately to several individuals who describe a similar ordeal. 12 to 15.000 left Srebrenica on 10 to 11 July. 5 to 6.000 crossed into BiH 2nd Corps-controlled territory in the southern Sapna area last night, 16 July. Up to 3.000 were killed on the way, mostly by mines and BSA engagements. Unknown others were captured. Some committed suicide. Unknown others went to Zepa." Now, I want to ask you, did you have occasion to encounter, if not perhaps this document, this information that up to 3.000 were killed on the way mostly by mines and BSA engagements, unknown others were captured, some committed suicide, unknown others went to Zepa? Did you have occasion to come across that type of information?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
