utterances.text: Yes, I do remember now this report from before, and I can say you see it's an early report from 17 July 1995, and it's -- you can see from this report it's an estimate, and based on evidence we have now, it was an estimate at the time, so how accurate again it is depends on different facts. So we don't have a background information how this number was obtained and from which sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, are we at the time for the break or do we still have five minutes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we have still five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then I'd like to move to another topic. As part of your investigation, sir, did you have occasion to conclude that there were a number of people killed, that is, a number of bodies in the town of Srebrenica itself, some of which are seen on various video-tapes from July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were some of them killed in Srebrenica town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to focus on those bodies for the moment. Did you ever come across any conclusive evidence confirming where those bodies from Srebrenica town were buried?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did, as part of your investigation, you come to a definitive number as to how many such bodies there were from Srebrenica town?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I still remember it wasn't many but there were few. You can even see them on videos.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that they probably would have been buried somewhere rather than being left in the open in Srebrenica town?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's really difficult to say where they would be buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My question -- perhaps you misunderstood. Not -- my question is not where they would be buried but would you agree with me that they probably would have been buried somewhere rather than being left in the open in Srebrenica town?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Probably everyone who dies will be buried or perhaps will not be buried. There is any factual information to your knowledge which allows you to give a better impression about what probably would have been the case? Do you have any information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, for this specific case in Srebrenica we don't have any information. I know for the Bratunac, for the killings in Bratunac, in school and around the Vuk Karadzic school the bodies were taken from there and from the stadium to Glogova mass grave. So it's possible that those bodies were taken there as well as part of the sanitation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you have no information.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But I have no information for the specific victims from Srebrenica town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Glogova. Am I correct that both Glogova 1 and 2 are the graves closest to Srebrenica town itself?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, primary, if you're talking about primary graves, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Now, in relation to the Glogova site, I would like to look at something with you, which is located at 1D1196, page 82, which should correlate to transcript page 33648.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could focus on lines 6 through 20, I'd like to examine those with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, you can follow along and it reads as follows: "Q. Another interesting point to discuss is the fact that the grave GL02-09 consists of a string of graves of various dimensions. This implies that graves of different sizes were being excavated according to the needs to dispose bodies therein and that there may have been a relative time difference between the excavation of each of the graves. At this point, it is not possible to precise what was the absolute time difference between each of the burial episodes. "Can you see that in front of you and do you agree with -- this is what Mr. Baraybar's report reads? "A. Yes, I see and I can agree. "Q. Now that we have read this passage, is it consistent with what Witness PW161 said and that we read a minute ago, that is to say that there were several burials at different times, which is also clear from the forensic evidence? "A. Yes, we can say something like that, yes." Can you confirm that the answers were accurately recorded in this selection of the transcript from the Popovic case?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you stand by those answers as truthful such that you would so testify here today if asked these same questions?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, now I believe we are at the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are, but I have one short follow-up question. Reading this, you were asked whether the report by Mr. Baraybar is consistent with what another witness said, a witness we do not know who that is and what he actually said but it's summarised here, and you said: "Yes, we can say something like that." So the question was whether two other witnesses are consistent in their statements and your answer is: "Yes, we can say something like that." Now, was -- did you mean to say that you share the views of those two other witnesses or at least the Baraybar report and Witness PW161, or did you just answer the question that the two answers are consistent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think the first one, Your Honour, that the views of those two other witnesses are consistent so that would be my -- but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you add anything that what you considered to be consistent opinions or views that you shared that view or that that is a possibility or what -- how do we exactly have to understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe we don't have the entire section here but in this particular case I know what -- what is all about. It's a separate grave in Glogova which was opened later, around 20 of July, so -- and this is consistent with what those two witnesses have been saying or this witness had been saying, that some bodies were buried in that particular site later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is that your view as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what I wanted to explore. We take a break of 20 minutes. Would you please follow the usher?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could I inquire with you on where we stand as far as time is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We are still on track, I believe -- I believe we might even be able to finish in the next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next session. Then we will take the break and we will resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you. I just wanted to ask about the scheduling of the next witness, a protected witness. Mr. Ivetic, I understand, is going to use most of this session. I may have about 10 or 15 minutes of redirect examination so it seems unlikely that we will reach him, or if so, just barely, and I was wondering whether or not it might be appropriate to discharge him at this time until tomorrow, as the witness is on stand-by presently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, can you be a bit more precise? Would it be 60 minutes or 50 minutes or?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's probably 45 to 50 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we could likely conclude the testimony of this witness by the next break. During the break we could have the protective measures organised and then we would still have half a session to start with the next witness. So I would rather keep him on stand-by, not promising anything at this moment, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to take a look with you, sir, at 65 ter number 18698 from the Prosecution's list in e-court. First off, sir, can you verify that this one-page corrigendum was authored by you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is the information in it true and correct, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in relation to the Kravica execution site and Glogova grave site, in the middle of this page you discuss a total of, I believe, 12 people in the first bullet point and 103 total people plus one truckload of bodies in the second bullet point as all being bodies from Glogova that cannot be attributed to the Kravica execution site. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You further conclude, and now I quote: "Nevertheless, considering the presented figures regarding the bodies buried in Glogova mass graves, as well as the above-mentioned different sources, most of these 1319 individuals must be still directly connected with the Kravica warehouse execution point. However, the exact number cannot be provided." Is that still your position?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this as the next available exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 18698 will be Exhibit D342.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D342 in the absence of any objection is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Janc, I'd like to stay at the Kravica site for a related topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And to do so I would bring up 1D1193 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now that we have it up on the screen I would ask that you take a look at it, it's dated 18 September 2001 and purports to be from field SOCO Tom Grange to chief forensic crime scene examiner. Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this document talks of artefact evidence being taken from Zeleni Jadar grave 6 to Kravica to try and compare and see if there is a match. It states that one piece with white paint recovered from the grave did not match anything at Kravica, but unfortunately that artefact was lost and could not be located for turnover back into the custody of the authorities. Do you have knowledge of this incident?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have any knowledge on that incident. It's just what we can read here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would this provide some indication that bodies from Kravica were mixed with bodies from some other source that is as of yet unknown at the Zeleni Jadar grave that is mentioned?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. Just based on one piece of artefact found in mass graves, because apart from that piece, there were many other artefacts found which could be linked with Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And that's why I ask you to please listen to my question.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know your question, what was your question, so if we can exclude based on that piece, you know, in Kravica warehouse, at least that's my understanding and what I could read during the course of my investigation, is that there was also a storage place before and many other artefacts might be collected during the sanitation area there after the mass execution. So it's possible that some other artefacts which have not been really linked with the construction itself may be also collected from the site itself and taken to secondary and primary and secondary graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That is one possible explanation. Is not another possible explanation that the bodies from Kravica were mixed with bodies from some unknown other source at Zeleni Jadar number 6?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know from evidence we have so far, that there is a certain number of individuals and that was exhibit which was just displayed before which had not originated from Kravica event, that's true. There --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And that was Glogova?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's Glogova, but Zeleni Jadar 6, it's a secondary grave to Glogova primary grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I presume since you were not aware of this incident you did not undertake to investigate anything in relation to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, can you investigate anything you're not aware of? Well, it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The witness is talking about other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, no, no --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- evidence. And I'd like to know did he investigate this with respect to other evidence or is he just now hypothesising.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you exclude any bodies from Zeleni Jadar from your report based on any concerns that they may have come from some other source that could not be determined?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I presented the number how many of those individuals have been found in Zeleni Jadar and I listed them in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this as the next available exhibit number in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number 65 ter 1D1193 will be Exhibit D343.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would now like to look at 1D1153 with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can please not broadcast that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a chart prepared by Ms. Svetlana Radovanovic, a Defence demographic expert, and was prepared and used in the Popovic case. And first of all, sir, am I correct that you can read and understand the portions of this chart that are in Serbo-Croatian on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And secondly, sir, do you recall being shown this data and this chart by the Defence during your testimony in the Popovic trial?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. I've been shown many of similar documents throughout my testimonies so it's possible this one was also presented to me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this was a list prepared based on preliminary information from the Bosnian Ministry of Defence that 137 persons who were registered as BiH soldiers and who were recorded as having been deceased in incidents prior to July 1995 were, in fact, included in the Prosecution's list of dead from Srebrenica with some of them being conclusively identified via ICMP DNA testing as being exhumed from the Srebrenica mass graves. Am I correct that your investigation did not undertake to review any records from the Ministry of Defence to ascertain if such -- if such preliminary information was true?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, you did not, or no, I'm not correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you're not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell me what efforts you undertook based upon information from the Ministry of Defence to ascertain if persons registered as having deceased or disappeared in incidents prior to July 1995 are included on your list?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, not many, but what I did was I consulted the demographic unit, the OTP demographic experts on this issue and they were the ones who in the name of the OTP requested further information from the Ministry of --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Defence?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Defence from the BiH on this issue. And I'm sure that they are going, this demographic experts were going to testify in this case and they would be the best source to answer these questions. However, as my understanding is that during their verification process, those individuals have been excluded or, you know, actually they concluded that there is no reliable source of information for such conclusion as you can see it here. And the fact that these individuals have been found in secondary and primary graves related to Srebrenica events would confirm quite opposite from my perspective because if, for example, and I think I did check some names, and I found that, for example, that they were found in a pile of bodies, so mixed together with bodies or victims from the Srebrenica events. So it's -- it would confirm quite opposite that these bodies are -- or these individuals have indeed passed away during Srebrenica events and not before. And the list which was compiled by the BiH Defence, as I'm told, was based on different sources and, you know, there were different reasons behind compiling such a list, so I'm not really aware anymore about exact particular reasons, but I know that as it was assessed by the demographic expert, this list hasn't been perceived as being really reliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's look at 65 ter 25923 on the Prosecution list.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: While we wait for it, I can tell you it's dated 2008 and arises from developments in the Popovic trial and is from a Ms. Ewa Tabeau. First of all, sir, is Ms. Tabeau the demographer that you consulted in answer -- that you identified generally in the answer to your -- the last question?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she is the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can, first of all, look at the first paragraph, does this appear to be the work that you just described generally that arose after this information was raised in the Popovic trial as to the preliminary information from the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 2 in the English and page 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down for the interpreters. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can focus on the third full paragraph from the top in the English, and it reads as follows: "Table 1 confirms that the per cent of the identified ABiH cases is relation to the identified OTP missing is about 70 per cent (exactly 71 per cent for ICTY sites and 73 per cent for all sites). Secondly, it points out that the number of identified ABiH cases exhumed from the ICTY grave sites (2686) is much larger than the number of identified ABiH cases from the non-ICTY grave sites (752; the sum of the two gives the overall total of 3438 identified ABiH cases). Basically about 78 per cent of all identified ABiH cases were exhumed from the ICTY sites as opposed to 22 per cent from non-ICTY sites." Sir, were you aware of this finding that about 70 per cent of the persons said to be victims of Srebrenica exhumed from ICTY sites were registered as members of the Armija BiH?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not about the exact number but I know there was a certain number of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we look at the bottom of page 2 of the English document, and this will be on page 4 in the B/C/S, it reads as follows: "Having said this, I checked inconsistencies in reporting of date of death/missing (DOD) for the ABiH records matched with the 2005 OTP list of missing persons. I was unable to compare place of death (POD) for those victims as POD is unavailable in the ABiH lists. A total of 220 ABiH records for those matched (5.371) with the OTP list have inconsistent DOD." It would thus appear that rather than the 137 that Ms. Radovanovic found, Ms. Tabeau found 220 cases with inconsistent data as to date of death from the ABiH lists and the Prosecution list. Were you aware of such information?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in that many details, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you take such information into account while preparing your new updated report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sure, I would -- and I did take this fact into consideration. Perhaps not in that way but what I included in my report were cases, individuals which were actually identified as being missing after the fall of Srebrenica and that they appear on the ICMP list. So whether or not now those 220 cases are included, I cannot tell you because I would need the names and I would need to compare it --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and it would take some time but it's possible. But, you know, as I explained just before, it would prove quite opposite when and where and how perhaps were these people executed, killed, or how they have died.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would like to look at another document on this topic with you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, inconsistencies is one issue but of course the next question, which is the correct information? Could the witness answer whether it was established whether either the -- your findings or the registered findings of the BiH Ministry of Defence were accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would now be just -- it would be a hearsay what I heard from the demographic expert. As I still remember, she was telling me that they were not reliable data. To what extent and to what and why, so we would need to consult -- I would need to consult her again and to see what she has to say on that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ivetic, I think that this report may contain some information, I don't know whether you want to tender this or not, but can the Chamber then also rely on information such as 127 have been corrected by the FPH Ministry of Defence in 2003? Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, and we are coming to the next -- the next document is also a follow-up to this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I found it in this document already on page 3, where the inconsistencies are to some extent resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: According to the OTP's demographer, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore I'm asking you whether we can rely on what is -- if you tender this document, whether we can rely on that information as well because if the document is tendered ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, he did not draft this document. I was thinking to save it for Ms. Tabeau but I -- it's up to the Prosecution if they want to tender it now. I don't know what weight it has now as to matters that this witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, I would specifically request that it be addressed with Dr. Tabeau who is a scheduled witness in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then it's -- should it then be marked for identification so that that we know that it has been dealt with --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- this witness. Then could we -- before we move to the next document, Mr. Registrar, could we assign a number for this document we MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. 65 ter number 25923 will be MFI D344.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And keeps that status and we will revisit matter, I do understand, when Ms. Tabeau appears to give her testimony. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The next document is number 25876 and I would ask that we please do not broadcast the same to comply with the non-disclosure of certain information on it that, as I understand, we still have not gotten approval to release.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a table prepared by Helge Brunborg, Ewa Tabeau, and Arve Hetland of the Prosecution demographic team and relates to these cases of persons for whom the dates of death provided problems, and Mr. Brunborg testified that this table reflected the corrected information or verifications sought from the BiH Ministry of Defence. And I propose to look at the last few entries on the first page of this chart and I think you could see that of those four, one is listed as having been exhumed at Branjevo, one exhumed at Cancari Road 3, and one at Rahunici. And I think you could see that the middle column is DOD -- I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are we at the bottom of the page? Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the middle column is DOD corrected and POD corrected. And if we look at the last four persons on this page of the list, the date of death has now been corrected as being 12 July 1995 instead of January 1994 as had been originally reported. Now, according to the letter from Ms. Tabeau and the section that Judge Orie just made reference to, this was enough for her to stop her review and conclude that this was a Srebrenica victim. But I would ask that you please look at the corrected POD, or place of death, that has now been verified by the BiH Ministry of Defence, and for these four, it is recorded as - and it's in B/C/S, I apologise to the translators but I'll be switching to B/C/S - [Interpretation] The Srebrenica-Tuzla road, Buljim village, Srebrenica-Tuzla road, Srebrenica-Tuzla road." [In English] Now, sir, can you confirm for me based on your investigations that these places and in particular Buljim refer to locations where the column of Srebrenica males engaged minefields and was engaged by the Serb forces in combat?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we were to look at this list in its entirety, I think we would see that for a great number of the instances where the dates have now been changed to July of 1995, the BiH ministry has also confirmed that the place of death is either the road from Srebrenica to Tuzla or the village of Buljim. Based on what you know, sir, can we on that bases exclude that these men perished from combat casualties or is the opposite true, that there is a considerable likelihood that they were in fact combat dead rather than executions?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know it's difficult to see and to conclude anything just based on this list because I would need to review it more formally and analyse all these sources and then to make a conclusion on that. It's -- you know, even whether or not now these individuals are indeed included in my report, I don't know from this list, so I would need to make additional inquiries so only that I would be able to respond. But if they are included into my report, you know, it's the proof that those individuals have been executed somewhere else than most probably initially reported as being killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you, the last part of your answer, initially reported as being killed. Being killed far earlier, is that what you wanted to refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct, as initially reported to the ABiH Ministry of Defence. So you would need to review all these sources more carefully and then to find out what is the problem. So I haven't been going into deep analysis of this list so I can't say. So in order to tell anything right now, I would need to review it more deeply.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I agree that there is more work that needs to be done to review these things to come to a conclusion, but I just want to make sure that you understood that the place of death that I read out is not the initial place of death that was incorrectly recorded. It's the confirmed place of death as reported by the Ministry of BiH when they in fact changed the date of death and responded to the inquiries of the Office of the Prosecutor to verify the initial information. Having that in mind, does your answer change?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really because I would need to see what was the reason for them to and what sources they were used in order to confirm certain facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now, I would like to look at one more name on the list without mentioning the name. It's the entry marked as ICMP 202/2 which is just three lines up from the first of the four individuals we were just looking at at the bottom of page 1. Here we see the notation that verification was requested and yet there is not any new date. Do you know if that means that verification verified the 1994 date of death for this person found in Zeleni Jadar number 5? Again it's ICMP --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- protocol number 202/02?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the entry. I'm just checking your question again. No, I don't really think I can answer you this question -- you know, this question, because it's the same problem, you know, about sources which were used for compiling this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. Then I'd like to move to another topic. Yesterday you testified about blindfolds and ligatures at transcript pages 15231 and 15230. Now, your report, P1987 MFI'd, dated June of 2013, I've looked through it and it only references one ligature found at Bljeceva 1, which is at page 24 of annex A, and 18 ligatures and four blindfolds as to Bisina, which is page 26 of annex A. And when I look at your previous reports, I also do not find any totals of additional blindfold and ligatures. So when you yesterday said that you had updated the numbers, is it -- were you updating numbers from your reports or were you perhaps updating the numbers from Dean Manning's year 2000 report as to blindfolds and ligatures? That wasn't clear to me so if you could please tell me which is it.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on top of the numbers or figures which were included in Dean Manning's report I also counted the blindfolds and ligatures which were found in subsequent years. So for that I have used -- I've reviewed the exhumation records on every single exhumation site, primary and secondary graves, so that's how I was -- I came up with the total figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And you'll agree with me that there are no total figures in your reports that you prepared from 2009 to present date?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are, you will find the total figures but they are wrong. They are actually -- now we have, I think, a double number.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now, Sunday evening we were provided with an information report arising from your proofing session with the Prosecution dated 18 August 2013. In that report, the Prosecution states as follows: "The witness reviewed his 2013 report, 65 ter number 30169, and confirmed its accuracy to his current information. The witness noted that his 2013 report does not present updated figures for blindfolds and ligatures recovered from Srebrenica-related grave sites and that these figures had not been updated. However, several graves have since been exhumed including two or three new individual graves and Zalazje 2 and Kaldrmica, included in the 2013 report. Both contain the remains of individuals appearing on the ICMP DNA match list, P01727, and the ICRC list of Srebrenica missing. The witness further noted that the number of blindfolds and ligatures reported by Manning in 2000 have substantially increased, see PO 1735, page 16." First of all, sir, is this information that I received from the Office of the Prosecutor correct and truthful?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are all of the additional blindfolds and ligatures that you testified about yesterday in fact coming from two or three new individual graves and Zalazje 2 and Kaldrmica?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in fact I haven't included any of ligatures or found any of ligatures and blindfolds in these two graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Then I need to know what other sites did you review that yielded the new additional blindfolds or ligatures that you are testifying about?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So these are all the sites along Cancari Road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All or just the ones that were excavated after 2000?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm adding is just the ones which were excavated after Dean Manning's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the same goes for all the secondary graves on Hodzici road, secondary graves in Liplje, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Great. That's what I was looking for, sir. Now, these additional ligatures and blindfolds that were the subject of your testimony yesterday from these locations, were they discovered loose in graves or were they affixed to bodies that were in the graves?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I still recall they were -- most of them were fixed to the bodies. Some of them were also loose but minority of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When you say minority of them are you referring to the ones that were loose?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, were these -- were any of these suspected blindfolds and ligatures discovered in areas surrounding the graves or at the surface rather than being buried at the same depth as the human remains?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall such instances. They were all found inside the grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And did I understand you correctly to say that the source that you reviewed was the exhumation records from the -- would it be the BiH authorities that did those exhumations?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, Dean Manning testified at this trial that he personally examined every artefact before concluding whether or not it could be included or excluded as a potential ligature or blindfold for purposes of his report. Did you perform that type of exhaustive physical review of the artefacts that you are testifying about?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't have that possibility because at the time, at that time, the graves were exhumed by the ICTY and I didn't have access to artefacts which were found by the BiH authorities during the exhumations they were conducting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm getting is information from the records which were provided to us on exhumation itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we take that your testimony is to additional blindfolds and ligatures updating Mr. Manning's 2000 figures, by my math that would mean that the additional grave sites which you mentioned which were exhumed from the year 2000 to present yielded a total of 145 additional suspected blindfolds. Does that number sound right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it may be. The total number now is 593.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I can tell you that at the time of Mr. Manning's report it was 448 as evidenced by P1734, page 1. Now, for these 145 additional suspected blindfolds, do you know how many were recovered affixed around the head or affixed to some other part of the body?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, as to ligatures, the same source, P1734, page 1, identifies that Mr. Manning found 423 suspected ligatures, and by my math, that would mean that with your figures, the graves that you mentioned that were exhumed post 2000, yielded 351 additional ligatures. Does that sound right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the total now is 774.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Now, based on your evidence yesterday, can we conclude that the vast majority of these 351 additional ligatures came from the Cancari site rather than being in relation to any of the other sites? I believe you mentioned yesterday 200-and-some from Cancari?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are from Cancari and Liplje sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Would be the majority of these?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And -- okay, you've already answered that you can't tell us except that a minority were found loose. Then I'd like to move to my last topic and my last few questions, sir, which is in relation to Godinjske Bare, and you testified yesterday at transcript page 15250 to 15252 about that location. You said this site was the execution and recovery site for six bodies killed by the Skorpion Unit and that this was roughly around 20 July 1995. Now, in this trial, Ms. Erin Gallagher from the Prosecution testified that the investigations that were conducted into this incident and the video cannot exclude the possibility that these particular killings occurred as late as 24 July 2013. And that's at transcript page 10136 to 10137. Would you defer to this formulation as being a more accurate description rather than what you said which was around 20 July?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's more accurate, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in relation to the so-called Skorpion video of this execution at Godinjske Bare, first of all, sir, have you had occasion to view the video in question?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you confirm for me that General Ratko Mladic is not present for any of the executions by the Skorpions of persons at Godinjske Bare?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you confirm that none of the participants in the video mention General Mladic as having directed or ordered these executions or that he would be apprised of the same?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to confirm that because it may be because I know that these members of the Skorpion Unit were arrested in Serbia after that and they testified about the incident, so if any of them referred to General Mladic as being the one who directed them, I cannot really --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the video, sir.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're talking about the video itself, no, that one is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in relation to the location, Godinjske Bare, that geographic location where these killings occurred and the bodies were found is, in fact, much closer to Sarajevo than it is to Srebrenica. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in fact, to travel to Godinjske Bare from Srebrenica, one would have to go either through or around Sarajevo first; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably, but I would need to consult the map and also we have to take into consideration, you know, the state on the ground at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Of course. Of course.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, as to the providence of this Skorpion video of this execution crime, am I correct that the same only became known to exist in the year 2003 and was obtained by the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal in 2004?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, for the last many, many questions, I wondered whether there was any dispute about those facts. When it was found, what, whether it's closer to Sarajevo, I mean is there any dispute about these matters? Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. There isn't a dispute about it but I don't know whether Mr. Ivetic is simply laying the basis for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, I was just asking you whether there was a dispute about it. Mr. Ivetic, I interrupted you when you started saying -- you started by saying, "Okay," and then you wanted to follow-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. My follow-up was going to be to thank the witness for his answers. I'm finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will -- I take it that will be appreciated by the witness. And it also confirms that it was not the basis for follow-up questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is one correction or, rather, I should ask for a clarification for the transcript. It's at page 68, line 19, and it's framed as part of the question that Mr. Ivetic put as to the date of the Skorpions killings. And he says as late as 24 July 2013, and I would assume that he meant 1995, but I'm not sure about that so I'd ask for a clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 1995. 1995. I apologise, I misspoke. It was an error on my part. It was intended as being 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I would ask the witness if that's how he understood my question and if his answer should be understood in that same manner?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I'm done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Vanderpuye, any questions in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I do have a few, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, quite briefly, you were asked a number of questions about combat-related casualties as concerns the contents of your report. Now, you've been an investigator in the Srebrenica crimes for a number of years. With respect to the locations where the primary mass grave sites are found, are you aware of any ongoing combat activity in and around the areas, those areas, at around the times that those executions occurred?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if I could have the assistance of the Registrar, I'd like to have P -- wait a minute. 65 ter 19221, please. I'm sorry, I'm mistaken. It's P1988. Apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This is the map that I showed you yesterday. The one that you prepared, in fact.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see the map on the screens but not on ours. There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to focus first on the top half of this map. That's quite good, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In the area of, at the very top, Pilica Dom, Branjevo military farm, are you aware of what evidence there is concerning the occurrence of combat activities in mid-July, specifically on or about the 16th and 17th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is no combat activities in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know where that area is relative to the defence lines of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's several kilometres away, so roughly 40, 50 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the area of Branjevo military farm and Pilica Dom, is it closer, well, where is it relative to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- Serbia is just across the border. It's just across the river on the right-hand side so a few kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What about the area of Kozluk? And there I'm referring specifically to the period of around 15 July 1995. During the course of your investigations, did you learn of any active combat activity that was occurring in that area or about that area on the 15th of July or around the 15th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What about the dam near Petkovci? Were you aware of any active combat activity that was occurring in that area on or around the 14th and 15th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the area of Petkovci and also for Orahovac, we can join them together, we can say that those two areas are closest to the areas where the combat activities were ongoing. But still far away. So I'm talking here of Baljkovica area which is left or west to those two execution sites.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say "far away," could you specify, was that five kilometres, ten kilometres? What is far away for one is nearby for another.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, let's say around 20 kilometres, maybe, away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that there was some combat-related activity occurring in the areas near -- nearest Petkovci and Orahovac. In the area of responsibility of what units, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you know, can you recall what specific battalions are in that area?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's 4th Battalion and 7th Battalion, 1st Battalion, but I'm not quite sure if I'm really precise on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not any casualties that were occurring there during the breakthrough of the column, whether the Muslim forces or people left behind their dead or took them with them to the extent that they could?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that some wounded members of the column had been taken with them and also I think some dead bodies have been taken with them to the free territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me move down the map, if I could, to some other areas. In the area of Glogova, Ravnice, can you tell us was there evidence of combat-related activity occurring in those areas?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Kravica execution site is the closest to the Pobudje area where we have the highest number of the surface remains found and I testified about how they were found. And now when we are all -- when you're asking me all the time about the combat activities so it's difficult to understand, you know, what do we all mean by the combat. So my understanding of the combat is fight between two -- two sides so -- but in case what happened, what was happening actually on the route, it's -- you know, it was raising my question all the time because every single trial so far I've been -- I'm asking the same questions about the combat activities in these areas. So my logic tells me that the combat activities is, you know, you are fighting, you know, between -- the two enemies or two sides are fighting. I'm not a military expert on this but I did a kind of research on this issue because I was always wondering, you know, if this is a real combat or is it just, you know, a way of telling what was -- what was happening on the ground because what would -- naturally everybody would expect that you have casualties on both sides, so and this is what I was trying to establish, you know. If there is a real fight, how many casualties would be on each side. And reviewing the records on war histories and everything, the ratio is if there is a real fight man on man, it's usually the casualties would be 50/50, or 40/60. So in cases where you have a dominant side, one side is stronger than the other, which was also I think the case in Srebrenica events, so then the ratio is -- is lower but still, let's say, 1.10. You would lose one of your soldiers for ten enemy soldiers. So if you apply this to the evidence in front of me, for example, if we say that people collected from the ground are casualties of combat activities, so we have 750 so far, it means on the other side, there should have been at least or around 70 dead Serb soldiers at the time so -- but we have minimal number of dead Serb soldiers at the time in the area throughout the passage of the column, so, and if we apply this further to the total number of individuals so far identified in these mass graves, which is 7.000, so if this was -- if this was coming out from the combat activities, that would be at least -- there should have been at least 700 Serb soldiers killed at the time, which it did not happen. So what we have here, we have a really low number of casualties on Serb side and a huge number on the other side. So my logic is telling me so this is not the combat at all, but, you know, it's only if one side is so dominant in these things, it's only possible that there were executions.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just bear with me one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have actually a quite a few number of questions, not an extensive amount of time but probably in the area of 15, 20 minutes, I think, and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What changes your position now, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What changes your position in a couple of minutes from -- I mean I consulted with you on what to do with the next witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and now you have --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's just that Ms. Stewart has informed me that it's time for the break. I can continue going but I just wanted to let you know that I have still a fair number of questions to ask. I don't think it will be substantially more than I estimated unless I've already exceeded it, but it's not my intention to go very long with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you limit yourself? I mean, we have to be very practical. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the Chamber is about to grant another ten minutes for Mr. Vanderpuye. Would that allow for continuing at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We agree to that. However, we already have three questions in recross coming from this, so in that instance, it's probably best to release the other witness if there is any -- I don't know how much Mr. Vanderpuye has for redirect yet to go, but I have no objection to another ten minutes but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will take the break now, and the next witness is excused for the day and we expect him tomorrow morning. But first, Mr. Janc should be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we resume at 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. I use the time meanwhile to deal with the following matter. The Chamber notes that the English and the B/C/S transcripts for the video Exhibit P521 do not fully reflect the conversations recorded in that video. The Chamber therefore instructs the Prosecution to upload complete English and B/C/S transcripts for this video exhibit reflecting the English subtitles contained in that video. And the Registry is also hereby instructed to make the necessary replacements once the corrected transcripts have been uploaded by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Janc, I was asking you about your understanding from your work on the Srebrenica investigation of what transpired in relation to certain combat-related activities while the column was moving from Srebrenica to the free territory. I think I had just begun to focus you on the lower part of this map and you were explaining about the area around Kravica warehouse and so forth. With respect to the movement of the column --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could just move to the top of the map once again. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With respect to the movement of the column through the RS territory to the BiH-controlled territory, do you have any information that any part of that column reached an area as high as, that is, as far north as, the Branjevo military farm or Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There is no such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Were you a member of the Office of the Prosecutor during the time that the battalion -- deputy battalion commander Lazar Ristic testified during the Tolimir case?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recall what Lazar Ristic said in respect of the casualties suffered by the Muslim side during the movement of the column through the area or within the area of the 4th and 6th Battalion on its way to the free territory?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really. You will have to jog my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If I may. In that trial, that is the Tolimir trial, on the 2nd of February, 2011, at transcript page 9300, beginning at line 8, on cross-examination by General Tolimir, he gave the following answers to the following questions. "Q. Witness, tell us" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, is this an introduction for follow-up questions or just whether the witness -- because the testimony of that witness, of course, should -- if that is one of the things you are aiming at, same question as I earlier put to Mr. Ivetic, are we supposed to rely on what that witness said or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'm going to ask Mr. Janc at the end of this is whether or not he took into consideration what he heard and what Mr. Ristic said regarding the disposition of those remains in his assessment of what were primary, secondary graves and what the relationship were -- what the relationship of those graves were -- was to those casualties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could we first ask the question in a very general way, whether apart from what the witness exactly said at the time, whether he -- this witness has considered that in his assessment because if the question is no, then we can move on right away, and if the question is yes, we could further explore the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, did you understand what Mr. President said?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you able to answer that question?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, because I'm not really sure what Mr. Lazar Ristic testified about so it's difficult for me to say or to state whether or not I have taken into consideration his statement as well, but most probably I did because this would be valuable information, whatever he said, regarding the disposition or movements of the bodies which were recovered.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Would it help refresh your recollection if I read to you what he stated during the course of his testimony?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, I would propose to read that portion of Mr. Ristic's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it's a short portion, then okay. If it's long, please summarise the gist of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The first part of it is relatively short and it's at page 9300, as I indicated, line 8, testimony from February 2nd, 2011. On cross-examination General Tolimir put this question to Mr. Ristic: "Q. Following the breakthrough by the enemy which breached your defence line, was it the Muslim army or the Serbian army that collected dead bodies? "A. Well, the Muslims collected theirs and the Serbs collected their own." Then he asked another question at line 16: "Q. Does this mean that the enemy soldiers gathered their dead and took them along as they passed through your territory? "A. I believe so. It was when we -- during this activity, we would receive word from our own soldiers of the casualties that we had, and wherever we went in the area of Baljkovica where the command post was situated and thereabout, we never came across a single Muslim casualty. "Q. As you were searching the terrain for casualties, did you find any Muslim victims in the area? "A. No." Do you recall that testimony of Mr. Ristic in relation to combat-related activities in the area of the responsibility of his battalion or thereabout?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, now I do recall it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you take that into consideration when you were assessing and reviewing the information concerning the designations of primary and secondary mass graves in relation to the Srebrenica incidents as reported in your 2013 update?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it corresponds exactly with the findings on the ground, that many people were never buried, their bodies were left behind and they were collected after so many years from the ground, from the surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'd like to show you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask the witness, do you know whether that witness, Mr. Ristic, I do understand, what army did he belong to? Because in order to understand his answer we should know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he belonged to the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And he said they never came across any Muslim victims when -- is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct. This is area north, near Baljkovica, so in that area -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's limited to that area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's limited to that area, yeah. But even in that area we do have some surface remains on the ground so -- but they are around that area and also we have a few, as we can see it on the screen now, we have a few smaller mass graves there, so there were some casualties in that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, you were asked a question by Mr. Ivetic on cross-examination relating to certain evidence of an individual, RM306, and that was with regard to communal graves. You might remember the discussion.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In your experience, in your investigation of this case, are you aware of any concerted efforts made by Serb forces, whether they be police or army, going into the woods, into the hills, to recover the remains of dead Muslims?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There are no such reports and we haven't -- or the investigation itself did not reveal any such information over the years.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you have any information with respect to the bodies that were recovered, in fact, by some Serb officials, whether they be civilian or military, that there were some bodies recovered and where they were recovered from?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It relates to the bodies along the Konjevic-Bratunac road.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we can just move on the map so we can have that area right in front of the Chamber to see it. And you'll have to blow up the area around Konjevic Polje. Yeah, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Janc. I didn't mean to interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, so this is one area where they were collected. Then we have the area around, and in the Vuk Karadzic school in Bratunac, stadium in Bratunac, so these areas were cleaned up.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Any information about similar activity going on by Serb authorities, civilian or military, up north in the Zvornik area?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And with respect to the bodies that were being recovered by Serb authorities along this Bratunac and Konjevic Polje road, in that area, where in that area relative to the road were those bodies recovered?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's my understanding that it was just next to the road, not far away from the road. They didn't go off the road very far into the woods but just along the road, according to my understanding, what you could see from the road itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: According to your investigations and what you've learned from the Srebrenica investigation in general, what -- is there anything that would have interfered with the capacity of the Serb forces, that is, the VRS, to collect bodies at or around the time that the Muslim column was passing through the area of Zvornik in the direction of the free territory?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were several activities going on at the same time. We know that after Srebrenica, the Serb forces went down to Zepa, they were engaged in that area, and soon after that also to Bihac area, so they were quite engaged at that time. And many forces were rerouted to those other parts of the country at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to show you P1481 very quickly. Let me just quickly ask you: Have you had a chance to review aerial images of mass grave sites related to the Srebrenica events?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to show you page 16, we'll start with, and we'll go --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This, for the record, reads "Orahovac, Lazete," and we'll go to page 17. And perhaps we can blow that up so that Mr. Janc can see the image.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this image, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's an aerial image from Lazete.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And what does it show?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the left-hand side it's dated 5th July 1995. We don't have any disturbances on the soil. And on the right-hand side, dated 27 of July, we have huge disturbances on earth.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me show you page 18. Do you recognise this image?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What does it show?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are dated first on the left-hand side 7 September 1995, again there is disturbances on the earth. And then on the right-hand side, 27 September 1995, we see changes on that same part of the earth, so that the soil was again disturbed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what does it show? Does it show a different grave or the same grave as the previous photograph? Or image?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I would have to check but it may be that these are two different, one is Lazete 2 and the other one Lazete 1. It's definitely Lazete 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me go to the next image on the following page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this image?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is from Lazete 2 site. It's more or less the same as we have seen it on the previous one. Disturbances and changes on the earth between 7 September and 27 September 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Have you reviewed images similar to this relative to the disturbed mass graves that are listed in your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And relative to those graves, are the dates that you can see disturbances on the aerial images the same or similar to the ones that I've just shown you relative to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are. They are either from beginning, end of September and also beginning of October, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you have a chance to review aerial images with respect to the secondary graves that are also listed in your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recall reviewing any graves associated with the -- any Cancari Road graves?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you were asked some questions about those secondary graves by Mr. Ivetic on cross-examination. I'd like to show you page 64 -- bear with me for one moment, please. Let's start by -- let me show you 65 first and then I'll show you 64. Do you recognise this image?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And has a designation CR1. Can you tell us what that denotes?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's Cancari 1, Cancari Road 1 secondary grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The date of this image is 2nd October 1995.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can I show you the previous page, page 64? Do you recognise this image?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the same spot. The picture is taken on 7th of September, 1995, and we have no disturbances on the soil, on the earth.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What does that suggest to you, in terms of the burial of combat casualties in that area on or around the time that the Muslim column was passing through that area on its way to the free territory as a primary grave, for example?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's obvious that those graves, secondary graves, have been opened at the same time as the primary graves and we even have, I think, several aerial images when we can see still graves being opened. I think this Cancari Road number 1 was already closed at the time, on that date of October, 2nd of October, 1995, it's already closed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could you tell the Chamber how much time you would need for further?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I have exactly 11 questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 11 questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I should be about 6 to 8 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm fine to leave it as it is, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we leave it as it is and we invite Mr. Ivetic to put any further questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, counsel. Further Cross-examination by Mr. Ivetic:

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sir, what written sources did you review for your testimony as to ratio of combat casualties, if any?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was actually an online review of various sources. It wasn't -- I didn't review many but this was just a quick review on what you can find on website.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did those articles that you reviewed relate to the type of combat described in the two Bosnian Muslim witness statements that we looked at today?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were different, actually different articles from different wars, so I didn't want to limit myself to specific event but I was just trying to get an idea how -- how many -- how these ratios would be presented over the years.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you consult with any military experts to reach or verify your conclusions as to ratio of combat casualties?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and I haven't, and that's what exactly I was, you know, trying to say, that I'm not a military expert on these things and my conclusion -- not conclusion but what I was able to find online can be verified, I'm pretty sure, by military experts.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: For minefields, would you expect the Serb side to have casualties on their side? For minefields experienced by the Bosnian Muslim column leaving Srebrenica, would you expect the Serb side to have casualties from those engagements?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they crossed them, that then would be casualties, yes, most probably. But I don't -- I don't have -- I don't remember there were instances, such instances during the takeover of Srebrenica or after.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: For incidences where the Bosnian Muslim column encountered shelling, would you expect casualties on the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And there were some casualties. I know for a few of them being killed in Kravica area. There were some casualties close to Orahovac, but not many. I know that the figure, the total figure of losses on VRS side was around 50, around 50, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did your research include looking into the status of civilians who joined a military column?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what sense, what do you mean if I have research -- what I found actually was the number included the ratio included also the number of civilians which were -- which were -- which suffered during those combats, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. At temporary transcript page 75, line 16 through 18, you are recorded as saying: "So my logic is telling me so this is not combat at all but, you know, if it's only one side is so dominant in these things, it's only possible that there were executions?" Is that a personal predisposition that you held at the time that you drafted your 2003 report that has been used in evidence today?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Actually not. I did research actually just recently, a few days ago, and it's just happened you know that coincides with -- coincided with what the other evidence -- evidence before this Tribunal are showing in relation to Srebrenica events.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I see. So this conclusion that I just read came to you between June 29th and today's date rather than coming from before?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Is it your position that surface remains were executions rather than combat casualties?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's everything. We have evidence on executions, we have evidence on combat casualties, we have evidence on suicides, and other causes of that, so it's about everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I thank you again for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I thank you for the indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Since the Chamber has no further questions for you, Mr. Janc, we would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you either by the parties or by the Bench, and we wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are excused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we adjourn I would like to briefly deal with a matter related to the three Rule 92 bis decisions. It is a follow-up by the Chamber in relation to three Rule 92 bis decisions which admitted a number of documents on the condition that the required Rule 92 bis attestations be filed. Even though the attestations were not filed, the Chamber reviewed them as uploaded into e-court by the Prosecution. And as a result, the Chamber now confirms admission of the following exhibits: P1904, P1909, P1911, P1916, P1918, P1919, P1921, P1924, P1931, P1933, P1935, P1938, P1940, and P1942, up to and including P1944. P1953 up to and including P1957. The Defence has not been given a specific opportunity to comment on the attestations which were uploaded into e-court. If there is any problem with the attestations, the Defence has an opportunity to ask the Chamber to revisit the matter, but in the absence of any such steps, the Chamber will -- the decision to admit these documents into evidence stands. Then we will adjourn for the day and we will resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 21st of August, 2013, at 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, III.
